transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-06
Start: 14:30 UTC
Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Marco Ruiz (Redwood SE), Dr. Samuel Briggs (CTO), Elena Petrova (Head of Security), Maj. Alex Turner (Program Manager)

Summary:
Discovery call focused on Valiant's requirements for an on-‑prem, air-‑gapped LLM inference deployment. Key concerns: offline updates, hardware procurement and constraints, encryption/KMS, auditability, and acceptable operational model (Redwood Private vs Dedicated vs hybrid). Action items and next steps agreed.

Topics:
- Air-‑gapped update workflow (signed packages / sneakernet)
- Hardware BOM and GPU availability (A100 vs H100 / quantized models)
- Key management (HSM / BYOK) and FIPS
- Network isolation, bastion jump hosts, and remote support under NDA
- Compliance: export controls, FedRAMP adjacency, SOC2/ISO requirements

Transcript (timestamps approximated every ~30s - imperfect auto transcription):
00:00 Lena Park: hey everyone thanks for joining, um we're excited to talk through your on-‑prem needs for running Redwood Private in an air-‑gapped enviro — environment, yeah
00:07 Dr. Samuel Briggs: thanks Lena, we appreciate it. quick context, Valiant handles classified telemetry analysis and anything that touches external networks is heavily restricted, so we are looking for a solution that can live entirely on our isolated cluster, no outbound internet.
00:18 Marco Ruiz: right, and just to set expectations, Redwood Private can be deployed in a fully offline mode; updates are shipped as signed artifacts, we support HSM integrations for keys and we have an offline update process we call "sneakernet" packages — physically transferred media.
00:28 Elena Petrova: can you spell out exactly how updates happen? we can't have any service phone-‑home even for metrics.
00:35 Marco Ruiz: absolutely. we provide a signed tarball that contains the runtime, model artifacts (or pointers for on-‑site model loading), and a verification manifest. your security team verifies signatures with your HSM or local KMS, you run the install on the secured nodes — no outbound required. There are also checksums and audit logs generated locally.
00:50 Maj. Alex Turner: do we need to recompile models on site? what's the requirement if we want to use H100 and some quantization?
00:57 Marco Ruiz: good question. most of the time we ship model artifacts pre-‑compiled for common kernels; for H100 we recommend the optimized build. if you have a highly restricted procurement window and different drivers/OS we can either cross-‑compile for you offline or provide a build pack you run in your CI that outputs validated kernels. there's some back-‑and-‑forth but it's doable.
01:18 Dr. Samuel Briggs: procurement is a big blocker — GPUs are on a long lead time. what's the minimum hardware to run a usable inference service for our use case (concurrent analysts ~12, latency <300ms for short prompts)?
01:28 Marco Ruiz: for that profile we'd usually recommend 2x H100 nodes with 80GB each in a multi-‑tenant pinned pool, but you can also achieve tradeoffs with A100-‑40 or 80GB depending on model quantization. if you use 4bit quantized weights and a smaller seq len you can fit more instances per GPU.
01:48 Lena Park: and we can run initial proof-‑of-‑concept on a single server to validate pipelines while you wait on procurement. the POC is usually throughput limited but shows correctness and functional parity.
01:56 Elena Petrova: what's the support model for in-‑person or remote troubleshooting if our cluster is air-‑gapped?
02:02 Marco Ruiz: we do remote support via presigned logs and triage bundles you export; for elevated support we can arrange cleared engineers to come on-‑site under NDA. there is an ops playbook we share. note on presigned logs — customers are often uncomfortable, but it's an opt-‑in export that stays on your network until you choose to share.
02:22 Dr. Samuel Briggs: ok, encryption — we require FIPS 140-‑2 validated crypto and enterprise HSM for keys. can Redwood integrate with our Luna HSM and support BYOK?
02:30 Marco Ruiz: yes, Redwood Private integrates with customer HSMs; we support PKCS#11 interfaces and can be configured to use your HSM for key wrapping of model encryption keys and TLS certs. we also support bringing your own keys (BYOK) and there is an offline key rotation procedure.
02:45 Maj. Alex Turner: how do you handle telemetry/observability without phone home? we still need cost and performance telemetry internally.
02:52 Lena Park: our console can run in a private control plane mode — everything is stored locally and dashboards are accessible only inside the network. For the hosted metrics you see in Redwood Console, we'll provide an on-‑prem variant that writes to your Prometheus/Grafana stack.
03:07 Elena Petrova: any dependencies on managed cloud services? we can't rely on cloud APIs.
03:11 Marco Ruiz: no mandatory cloud dependencies. the control plane can be self-‑hosted and we ship containerized services. some optional features like model catalog syncing are offline too — you download the catalog bundle.
03:21 Dr. Samuel Briggs: what about model updates cadence? We have policy that requires a cryptographic review for every model update.
03:28 Marco Ruiz: you can gate updates. we support signed model artifacts and delta bundles; you can require manual approval. for audits we provide a signed changelog and reproducibility metadata.
03:40 Lena Park: also wanted to flag rollout policies — can do canary onboardings in restricted subnets and automatic rollback based on local evals.
03:48 Maj. Alex Turner: on the topic of evals, we need a way to run offline regression tests against our prompt sets. can Redwood run eval sets locally?
03:55 Marco Ruiz: yes, our eval harness is distributable; we provide a test runner that executes prompts, generates metrics and stores results in a local DB for later review.
04:05 Elena Petrova: compliance: do you have customers in defense or gov that followed similar patterns?
04:10 Lena Park: yes — we've deployed to regulated defense contractors and cleared labs under similar constraints; we can share redacted case studies and references under NDA.
04:18 Dr. Samuel Briggs: two big risks for us: export controls on certain models and chain-‑of-‑custody for model training data. does Redwood host models that might be restricted?
04:27 Marco Ruiz: we curate a model catalog and can exclude specific models from the bundle you receive. if there's export control risk we can provide a vetted, on-‑prem only model artifact. chain-‑of-‑custody — we provide provenance metadata but deep training lineage is something we coordinate with your legal and policy teams.
04:44 Lena Park: quick price note — private on-‑prem pricing is an annual license plus support uplift for the air-‑gapped workflows and cleared engineer time for on-‑site work. we'll follow up with a tailored cost estimate.
04:56 Maj. Alex Turner: any blockers on our side to start a pilot? we need a non-‑production server and approval from security to accept external signed artifacts.
05:03 Dr. Samuel Briggs: security will want to review the signature verification process and the packaging. Elena will lead on that.
05:08 Elena Petrova: yep we'll need a sample package and the verification docs; also sample HSM integration steps.
05:15 Marco Ruiz: action: I'll produce a BOM for pilot hardware and a sample signed package walkthrough.
05:20 Lena Park: I'll send SOC2 / ISO docs and the on-‑prem architecture deck; also a short checklist for procurement.
05:26 Dr. Samuel Briggs: timeline — procurement might take 6-‑8 weeks, we'd like to align a POC that can start with a single server in-‑lab by mid-‑Jan if possible.
05:34 Lena Park: understood — we'll aim to have the pilot estimate and docs by next week so you can start procurement.
05:40 Maj. Alex Turner: one small thing — can you confirm support for air-‑gapped container registry flows? we use an internal registry behind ECR-‑like interface.
05:47 Marco Ruiz: yes we support OCI images and can produce tarball exports compatible with your registry importer; we also support signed container images using cosign.
05:55 Dr. Samuel Briggs: ok this was helpful, thanks.
06:00 Lena Park: great — recap of next steps: Lena sends compliance/security docs, Marco sends BOM and sample package walkthrough, Sam/Elena share network diagram and compliance checklist, schedule on-‑site demo week of 12/14. Any other Qs?
06:12 Elena Petrova: not at the moment, thank you.
06:15 Maj. Alex Turner: thanks, bye.
06:18 Meeting end.

Notes on transcription quality: automatic transcript had a few mis-‑heard terms (e.g., 'K V cache' instead of KV cache; 'kuburnetes' for Kubernetes) and some speaker attribution errors early in the call. The body above preserves conversational artifacts and filler words.
